title: Interview Cop | Follow-up questions for coding interviews
excerpt: Ask about the code on the shared screen, or practice explaining your own.
content_html:
For hiring teams and candidates

Stop interviewing
ChatGPT.

Because you want to see how they think

Capture code from any of these

CodeSignal·HackerRank·CoderPad·LeetCode·Shared screens

The tests pass.
What would you ask next?

Pick one line of code and ask the candidate to explain it.

How it works

Take a screenshot when the code changes

Keep the app beside the shared editor. Only the interviewer needs it on the call.

Save the task and code

Click Start to capture the task. Click Next to capture the code.

Get questions

Click Run Cop, then the arrow to see your questions.

Ask one

Pick a question and let the candidate talk you through the code.

During the call

What would you ask about this lookup?

Select the function

Capture the function that looks up a transaction.

Read the question

Run Cop suggests a question about the lookup.

Try an example

Ask what happens when two keys land in the same bucket.

Question 2 · read out loud~1 min

“In processTransaction, how does the map find the right transaction if two keys land in the same bucket?”

Listen for

The map compares the keys. If it uses chaining, it may check several entries in that bucket.

Right

Wrong

What the interviewer can work with

Keep the first draft

Save the code before the candidate changes it. Ask what changed and why.

Problem statement

Capture 1

First draft

Capture 2

Revised code

Capture 3

Ask about a line of code

Each question points to a detail in the screenshot, like a function or an if statement.

Map lookup

Q1

Duplicate keys

Q2

Empty input

Q3

Know what to listen for

Each question comes with a short suggested answer.

Why use a hash map?

What happens with duplicate keys?

What happens if the input is empty?

Give the candidate a place to start

Pick a small input. Ask the candidate to show what their function does with it.

How hiring teams use Interview Cop

Ask about the code on the call. Bring an example to the team discussion afterward.

Engineering managers

Discuss a code choice

Show the team the code and explain why the candidate chose that approach.

Technical interviewers

Find a follow-up

When the candidate changes the code, capture the new version and ask why.

Candidates

Practice explaining your code

Open a problem you’ve solved. Answer a question out loud, then check the suggested answer.
